takeaway: The third part of the axillary artery, from pectoralis minor to teres major, gives off the subscapular, anterior circumflex humeral and posterior circumflex humeral arteries.

question.text: The axillary artery is conventionally divided into three parts, each giving off its own branches. The third part divides into which of the following branches?

answer.text: Subscapular, anterior circumflex and posterior circumflex humeral arteries

lines.text: The axillary artery begins at the border of the first rib and has three parts.
The first part ends at pectoralis minor, giving off the superior thoracic artery.
The second part lies deep to pectoralis minor, giving the thoracoacromial and lateral thoracic arteries.
The third part runs from pectoralis minor to the lower border of teres major.
It gives off the subscapular artery,
and the posterior circumflex humeral artery.
lines.say: and the posterior circumflex humeral artery. (sigh)

lines.text: So the answer: subscapular, anterior and posterior circumflex humeral. The lateral thoracic and superior thoracic come earlier.
